sources.entry: The eXpress Data Path - Measures an in-kernel programmable path against DPDK and the stack per core, with the full configuration published.

summary.one_liner: Source repository for the CoNEXT 2018 paper on the eXpress Data Path (XDP), including the LaTeX source, datasets, benchmark notes, and slides.
summary.what_it_does: This repository holds the LaTeX source, datasets, and experimental notes for the paper "The eXpress Data Path: Fast Programmable Packet Processing in the Operating System Kernel," presented at ACM CoNEXT 2018. It includes a compiled PDF of the paper and org-mode source for the presentation slides, which can be exported with the org-reveal Emacs plugin. The benchmarks directory contains org files with setup instructions for running the XDP and DPDK experiments. The README points to a specific upstream Linux kernel branch (xdp_paper01) and commit used for the tests, though the commit link is truncated in the text. The README describes the test hardware: an Intel Xeon E5-1650 v4 workstation with two Mellanox ConnectX-5 dual-port 100Gbps NICs, with load generated from other machines.
use_cases: compare XDP against DPDK packet processing
read the eXpress Data Path research paper
find experimental setup notes for XDP
reuse paper slides for a talk on XDP
notable: Full experimental notes for XDP and DPDK setups in the benchmarks/ directory
Presentation slides maintained as org-mode source
Test hardware described: Xeon E5-1650 v4 with two ConnectX-5 100Gbps NICs
Source code and text released under GPL v2 and CC-BY-SA
caveats: The README's source-code commit link is truncated, so the exact upstream commit is not recoverable from the text
Reproducing the experiments requires familiarity with Linux and 100Gbps NIC hardware
The repository is paper and benchmark material, not a packaged XDP tool
summary.license: GPL v2 for source code; CC-BY-SA for text and figures
